L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The BIR number (Board of Inland Revenue file number). Types include the Individual Income Tax File Number, Company File Number, PAYE number and VAT registration. A self-employed person or sole trader must register for a BIR file number. Individuals can register online through e-TAX with form IA-001 and valid ID, and the number must appear on returns and most tax correspondence (Inland Revenue Division).

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 12.5%; exports, basic foodstuffs and other qualifying items are zero-rated. Register once commercial supplies reach TTD 600,000 in the preceding 12 months, or when there is evidence that supplies will exceed that in a 12-month period (Deloitte 2026). Whether services to foreign clients count as zero-rated exports was not confirmed.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
